structured_output.summary: ExoFOP now lists TOI 7928.01 on this star; the signal is no longer new.
reasons: The signal is no longer new: `exofop_tois` is "TOI 7928.01". The verification record shows the cross-match found no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-09 through 2026-10-29, so the TOI was issued after 2026-10-29, after the earlier 'proposed for submission' decisions of 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-20 in the record. A CTOI must be new, and a TOI on the star removes that.

The input does not give the period of TOI 7928.01, so I cannot cite a period match directly. But the star shows one very strong transit signal (`MES` 38.93774, `joint_search_snr` 62.5, `fit_depth_ppm` 3138 on a `tmag` 10.0672 star), and a TOI issued on this star in the weeks after Sector 98 is almost certainly this signal. If the person checking finds TOI 7928.01 has a different period, the candidate should be re-examined rather than dropped.

I agree with the mechanical decision 'proposed for drop' (ExoFOP has TOI [TOI 7928.01]). Nothing in the data argues against the signal itself: `pixel_verdict` on target in both sectors (`pixel_verdicts_by_sector` S32 SNR 10.9, S98 SNR 7.7, best star TIC 264626874; `joint_difference_image_snr` 13.4), and both difference images peak on the target pixel with the free-fit cross on the target.

The transit is physically consistent with a companion of the target: `stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio` 0.971, `fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis` 1.11, `odd_even_difference_sigma` 1.30, `secondary_depth_ppm` -18 +/- `secondary_depth_error_ppm` 34 against `secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm` 157, `transit_grazing` False with `fit_impact_parameter` 0.744 +/- `fit_impact_parameter_error` 0.0346, giving `planet_radius_earth_radii` 17.66 +/- `planet_radius_error_earth_radii` 0.90, below the 22.4 stellar threshold. The all-sector figure shows a flat-bottomed transit with sharp ingress and egress in both S98 and S32 and nothing at phase 0.5. None of this changes the drop; it only means the drop is on grounds of prior listing, not of a false positive.

The only caution, 'neighbour able to cause dip' (`gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip`: Gaia DR3 3237833152757788800 at 27" G 15.5 needs 24%; Gaia DR3 3237833187117523712 at 57" G 15.6 needs 27%), is answered by the on-target pixel verdict and by TRICERATOPS `nfpp_mean` 0 with `nearby_scenarios_excluded` True and `most_likely_scenario` TP on TIC 264626874 (`fpp_mean` 0.1692 +/- `fpp_standard_deviation` 0.13, `triceratops_verdict` likely planet). It is not a reason to drop.

The ellipsoidal caution that drove the two 'held' decisions of 2026-10-16 in the record no longer applies: the current step 9 gives `ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm` 162 +/- `ellipsoidal_amplitude_error_ppm` 111 (1.5 sigma), `ellipsoidal_companion_mass_solar_masses` empty, step 9 `cautions` empty; `gaia_rv_variable` False, `gaia_ruwe` 1.19, `gaia_non_single_star` 0. So there is no evidence of a stellar companion; the drop is solely because the TOI already exists.

Why not 'held': `released_tess_sectors_not_in_all_sector_verification` is empty, and `unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star` 110 cannot change the fact that TOI 7928.01 is already listed. More data cannot make the signal new again, so a hold would serve no purpose.
